To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RNase L-generated small dsRNAs promote a switch from RNase L-induced, autophagy to RNase L-induced apoptosis by caspases-mediated cleavage of the autophagy protein Beclin-1 that terminates autophagy and enhances apoptosis by translocation of the cleaved Beclin-1 to mitochondria.
RNase L generated dsRNA promotes a switch from autohagy to apoptosis by cleaving Beclin-1 to terminate autophagy and induce apoptosis.
small RNAs generated by RNase L activate apoptosis in virus-infected and tumor cells by cleavage of the autophagy protein Beclin-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the endoribonuclease RNase L in the regulation of cell death and autophagy.
the mechanism of crosstalk between autophagy (cellular self-degradation) and apoptosis (cell death) that is induced by a cellular antiviral enzyme, RNase L, during viral infection.
the mechanisms that regulate cell death in response to virus infection and how these mechanisms are exploited by cancer cells to survive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNase L generated dsRNAs promote a switch from the autophagy pathway to the apoptosis pathway by cleaving Beclin-1 and inhibiting autophagy, thereby promoting cell death.
RNase L cleavage products promote switch from autophay to apoptosis in a caspase dependent manner by cleaving Beclin 1.

RNase L cleaves viral and host RNA, generating small RNAs that activate caspases and promote apoptosis by cleaving Beclin-1 and terminating autophagy, and that apoptosis and autophagy inhibit each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new role of RNase-L generated small RNAs that promote apoptosis by caspases cleavage of Bechin-1.
